text: Jaffle Shop's governed platform is five layers, stacked in a specific order, each one standing on the layer built before it. This lesson plans all five before any of them get built.

The stack is Snowflake first, for warehouses, roles, and schema separation; then dbt, for the transformation and governance layer; then Python for ingestion; then CI/CD as the merge gate; and finally Power BI on top.

Snowflake gives dbt a role to run as and a RAW schema to read from. dbt then turns that raw data into trusted marts through staging and intermediate models, a snapshot, and a real set of tests and documentation.

Python handles the one gap dbt can't close itself — loading a one-off external source with no native connector. CI/CD makes sure dbt build passes before any change merges. And Power BI connects only to PROD's marts, never RAW, never DEV — a deliberate governance boundary, not an afterthought.

Each layer depends on something real the one before it produced — that's why the build order isn't arbitrary. Chapter 2 starts at the bottom of the stack: Snowflake warehouses, roles, and the RAW, DEV, and PROD schema split.
